## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)). I cannot set labels from a fork; suggested: `cat-bugfix`, `area:sparse_attention`, `op: DSA`, `mod-cutedsl`, `orig-nv-eng`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

Fix out-of-range indices from the varlen DSA indexer top-k kernel when a row is shorter than its
misalignment prologue: `prologue_elems` is clamped to the row length. Adds an L0 regression test.

## Why

`IndexerTopKKernelVarlen` splits each row into a scalar prologue up to the next 32-byte-aligned
address, a vectorized body and a tail. `prologue_elems` comes from the row address alone and is not
bounded by `length`. When a row starts misaligned (bf16 with `num_cols % 16 != 0`, fp32 with
`num_cols % 8 != 0`) and its `seq_len` is smaller than the prologue, the prologue reads columns past
`seq_len` and can select them, so the kernel returns indices >= seq_len (`remaining` also goes
negative). Downstream sparse attention then gathers KV entries outside the row's valid range.

Repro (B200):

```python
x = torch.randn(2, 17, device="cuda").bfloat16()
x[1, 3:] = 100.0
seq_lens = torch.tensor([17, 3], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
r = DSA.indexer_top_k_wrapper(x, seq_lens, top_k=1, next_n=1, return_val=True, tie_break=1)
r["indices"][1, 0]  # 3 -- outside seq_len=3
```

Conditions: misaligned row start, `seq_len` < prologue elements, and `top_k < seq_len`. Clamping keeps
the existing split for every row at least as long as its prologue; a shorter row becomes all prologue
(empty body and tail), which is the correct scalar path. Same family as #410 (OOB lanes in varlen
indexer top-k).

## Related issues

Related to #410.

## API and compatibility impact

None. No API change; aligned rows and rows longer than their prologue take the same path as before.

## Testing

B200 (sm_100), CUDA 13.4, torch 2.15, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8, this branch on develop d0c3db0a,
installed with `pip install .` (conftest banner confirms the tested tree):

- RED: with the develop version of `indexer_top_k_varlen_util.py`,
  `pytest deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_DSA_indexer_top_k.py -k short_misaligned_row`
  -> 2 failed (`assert 3 < 3`).
- GREEN: `pytest deepseek_sparse_attention/cutedsl/test_DSA_indexer_top_k.py` -> 104 passed (L0);
  with `-m "L0 or L1 or L2 or L3 or L4"` -> 128 passed.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: black / SPDX passed, no changes.


cc @Anerudhan @jiayus-nvidia

detail.title: DSA indexer top-k: clamp the misaligned-row prologue to the row length

files.patch:
@@ -490,6 +490,9 @@ def indexer_topk_kernel_per_row(
             fix_bytes = align_bytes - misalign
 
         prologue_elems = cutlass.Int32(fix_bytes // elem_bytes)
+        # A row shorter than the bytes up to the next aligned address is all prologue.
+        if prologue_elems > length:
+            prologue_elems = length
 
         remaining = length - prologue_elems
         aligned_size = (remaining // self.vec_size) * self.vec_size

@@ -221,3 +221,28 @@ def test_DSA_indexer_top_k_wrapper_ignores_vector_padding_with_negative_infinity
         return_val,
         tie_break=tie_break,
     )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L0
+@torch_fork_set_rng(seed=0)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype,num_cols", [(torch.bfloat16, 17), (torch.float32, 9)], ids=["bf16", "fp32"])
+def test_DSA_indexer_top_k_wrapper_short_misaligned_row(dtype, num_cols):
+    """A row shorter than its misaligned prologue must not read columns past its length."""
+    try:
+        from cudnn import DSA
+    except ImportError:
+        pytest.skip("Environment not supported: cudnn[cutedsl] not installed")
+
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] < 9:
+        pytest.skip("Indexer top-k requires compute capability 9.0 or newer")
+
+    seq_len = 3
+    top_k = 1
+    # Row 1 starts num_cols elements in, which is not 32-byte aligned; its prologue would span past seq_len.
+    input_values = torch.randn(2, num_cols, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda").to(dtype)
+    input_values[1, seq_len:] = 100.0
+    seq_lens = torch.tensor([num_cols, seq_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+
+    result = DSA.indexer_top_k_wrapper(input_values, seq_lens, top_k=top_k, next_n=1, return_val=True, tie_break=1)
+    assert int(result["indices"][1, 0]) < seq_len
+    check_ref_indexer_top_k(input_values, seq_lens, top_k, 1, result["indices"], result["values"], True, tie_break=1)
